title: Question 1.1
statement_text: For which graphs $F$ is there an $F$-counting lemma in $C_4$-free graphs?
context_text: For a graph $F$, the authors make the notion of an $F$-counting lemma in $C_4$-free graphs precise as follows: $F$ is countable if for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that whenever $G$ is an $n$-vertex $C_4$-free graph on vertex set $V$ and $H\in[0,1]^{V\times V}$ is a symmetric matrix (an edge-weighted graph) with $\left|\frac{e_G(A,B)}{n^{3/2}}-\frac{e_H(A,B)}{n^2}\right|\le\delta$ for all $A,B\subseteq V$ (where $e_G(A,B)$ counts pairs $(x,y)\in A\times B$ with $xy\in E(G)$ and $e_H(A,B)=\sum_{x\in A,y\in B}H(x,y)$), then for every family $(A_v)_{v\in V(F)}$ of subsets of $V$ one has $\frac{\hom_{\mathbf{A}}(F,G)}{n^{|V(F)|-|E(F)|/2}}\ge\frac{\hom_{\mathbf{A}}(F,H)}{n^{|V(F)|}}-\epsilon$, where $\hom_{\mathbf{A}}(F,G)$ is the number of homomorphisms of $F$ to $G$ mapping each $v$ into $A_v$ and $\hom_{\mathbf{A}}(F,H)=\sum_{x_v\in A_v}\prod_{uv\in E(F)}H(x_u,x_v)$. This is a one-sided (lower-bound) sparse counting lemma, the scaling coming from the fact that $C_4$-free graphs have at most $(1/2+o(1))n^{3/2}$ edges; countability of $F$ yields an $F$-removal lemma in $C_4$-free graphs. In earlier work the authors proved that $C_5$ is countable. Here they show that every countable graph has girth at least $5$ (using the polarity graph), that trees and all cycles of length at least $5$ are countable, that adding a pendant edge preserves countability, and they give a recursive 'islands and bridges' construction producing many countable graphs of girth at least $5$ (e.g. chains of $5$-cycles and subdivisions of cliques), but they are far from a classification. They also note that it seems necessary that every subgraph $F'$ of $F$ satisfies $|E(F')|\le2|V(F')|-4$, which would imply that $d$-regular countable graphs have $d\le3$.

title: Open Problem 2.17
